open_points.subject: A16 rule 4 vs A20 ceiling for implementation code
open_points.text: A16 rule 4: "...a text field over `bounded_text_bytes_max`, or implementation code over `implementation_code_bytes_max` is refused." A20 sets `bounded_text_bytes_max` = 16384 and `implementation_code_bytes_max` = 1048576.
open_points.question: Is implementation code exempt from the generic text-field limit, or must it satisfy both limits (making the 1 MiB ceiling unreachable)?
options: Implementation code is checked only against `implementation_code_bytes_max`.
Implementation code must satisfy both limits, so effective max is `bounded_text_bytes_max`.
`bounded_text_bytes_max` applies to all text fields except specific schema-designated exceptions, which must be listed.
open_points.default_guess: Treat implementation code as a specific exception and enforce only `implementation_code_bytes_max` for that field.

open_points.subject: Authority recorded for `draft-write` attempts (A10, A11, M26)
open_points.text: M26: authority is "the approval or the grant it used, or for a `draft-write` send the flow activation..."; A10 rule 6: "A `draft-write` send records as its authority the FlowActivation..."; A11 rule 1: for non-read operations, EffectAttempt is written "naming the approval or grant it uses".
open_points.question: For `draft-write` sends, especially resend-after-`not_applied` where A10 requires a fresh approval, which authority must be recorded in EffectAttempt: FlowActivation, approval/grant, or both?
options: Always record FlowActivation for `draft-write`, even when a fresh approval was required.
Record approval/grant when used; otherwise FlowActivation.
Record both (requires model/rule change to allow dual authority fields).
open_points.default_guess: Record approval when one is required/used; otherwise record FlowActivation.

open_points.subject: Request refusal precedence during token-list reread failure (A16 rules 1 and 2)
open_points.text: A16 rule 1 defines first-failing order starting with request size and token checks. A16 rule 2 says when token-list reread checks fail, "every request is refused... with the same one refusal as an unknown token (rule 1)".
open_points.question: When token-list reread is in failed state, do other early refusals (oversize request, unknown operation/schema errors) still take precedence, or must every request return the single unknown-token-style refusal regardless of content?
options: Global fail-closed mode: always return the single unknown-token-style refusal.
Still apply rule-1 ordering; unknown-token-style refusal only for auth-related failures in that state.
Apply size limit first, then single unknown-token-style refusal for anything within size.
open_points.default_guess: Use global fail-closed mode and return the same unknown-token-style refusal for all requests until reread succeeds.
